issues.label: Jurisdictional-priority rule application
issues.why: The court must determine whether Wendee's first-filed, first-served Franklin County complaint gives it priority over the Perry County case.

issues.label: Interaction of venue and priority rule
issues.why: The court must decide whether improper venue defeats the jurisdictional-priority rule or whether priority controls regardless of venue propriety.

issues.label: Whether venue is jurisdictional
issues.why: Venue defects generally do not deprive a court of subject-matter jurisdiction, affecting the proper remedy for improper venue.

issues.label: Proper remedy for improper venue
issues.why: Civ.R. 3(D) requires transfer, not dismissal, when venue is improper, so dismissal may have been erroneous.

issues.label: Civ.R. 3(C)(9) ninety-day residency application
issues.why: The court must apply the 90-day residency provision to determine whether Franklin County was a proper venue.

issues.label: Availability of other venue bases
issues.why: Civ.R. 3(C) provides multiple non-exclusive venue grounds beyond (C)(9), such as where the claim arose or defendant's business.

issues.label: Complaint's pleaded venue allegations
issues.why: Wendee alleged the claim arose and Robert's business was in Franklin County, which could independently establish venue.

issues.label: Perfection of service in Franklin County
issues.why: Whether and when service was perfected determines when the Franklin court acquired priority.

issues.label: Timing of competing filings
issues.why: Franklin was filed April 1 and Perry April 7, making the earlier filing potentially controlling.

issues.label: Whether cases involve same parties and claims
issues.why: The jurisdictional-priority rule requires the two actions to concern substantially the same matter.

issues.label: Civ.R. 12(B)(2) lack of jurisdiction basis
issues.why: The court must assess whether Robert's personal jurisdiction argument has any independent merit.

issues.label: Effect of Perry County's prior ruling
issues.why: The Perry court already ruled venue proper there, raising comity, collateral estoppel, or conflicting-order concerns.

issues.label: Effect of Fifth District's dismissal
issues.why: The appellate mootness dismissal and finding of adequate legal remedy may bear on how the venue dispute is resolved.

issues.label: Fairness/unfairness under trial court's standard
issues.why: The trial court conditioned applying Civ.R. 3(C)(9) on it not creating unfairness, requiring a fairness analysis.

issues.label: Risk of conflicting jurisdiction between counties
issues.why: The court must avoid two courts simultaneously exercising jurisdiction over the same divorce.

issues.label: Proper venue in divorce actions specifically
issues.why: Domestic-relations venue rules and residency requirements may apply differently than general civil venue.
